title: Affine tilde comparison for one positive homogeneous graded-module chart
statement: Let $S$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded commutative ring with grading $\mathcal A$, and $M$ a $\mathbb Z$-graded $S$-module with internal grading $\mathcal M$ compatible with scalar multiplication. Set $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj]. Index charts by pairs $f=(a,d)$ with $d>0$ and $a\in S_d$, put $D_f=D_+(a)$, $R_f=S_{(a)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and let $Z_f$ be submodules of $M_a$ whose carriers are precisely the equal-degree fractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Suppose additive maps $\rho_{f,g}:Z_f\to Z_g$ and ring maps $\rho^S_{f,g}:R_f\to R_g$ are given for every $D_g\subseteq D_f$. Suppose each inclusion admits a homogeneous relation $g^e=bf$ with $e>0$, each $\rho$ is semilinear over $\rho^S$, and for every such relation it sends $y/f^m$ to $b^my/g^{em}$. Assume identities, composition and bijectivity when chart opens coincide. Assume moreover every ring restriction is induced by a ring map $S_f\to S_g$ commuting with $S$. Let $F$ be any sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with additive identifications $F(D_f)\cong Z_f$, scalar compatible via awayToSection and restriction compatible with $\rho$. Then, for each positive homogeneous chart $f$, the restriction $F|_{D_f}$ is isomorphic as an $\mathcal O_{D_f}$-module to the restriction of $\widetilde{Z_f}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] along the canonical isomorphism $D_f\cong\operatorname{Spec} R_f$ [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection]. The conclusion is an affine chart comparison, not an assertion of global quasi-coherence.

proof.text: Pull back the principal-open basis of Spec R_f through basicOpenIsoSpec. PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens and the induced homeomorphism prove that these opens form a basis of D_f, including an empty chart.

Apply gradedModuleAwayRestriction to obtain its submodules and localization comparisons. Equality of the carriers from hZ identifies the constructed submodules with the specified Z. For each chart inclusion choose the homogeneous relation from hlaws. Represent an arbitrary localized module element as y/f^n and compare the two fraction formulas; subtype injectivity proves rho agrees with the constructed restriction. hcanonical and IsLocalization.ringHom_ext identify the ambient ring map with lambdaS; val_injective identifies rhoS. These equalities give the theta and thetaS hypotheses of the sectionwise comparison theorem.

Apply gradedModuleChart_basisComparison to the aligned theta and thetaS, the canonical ring maps, and alpha with its scalar and restriction compatibility. This gives compatible linear equivalences between the restricted module sheaves on the principal-open basis.

Extend the additive maps on the basis using restrictHomEquivHom. To check linearity on any open, restrict the two scalar expressions to a basis neighbourhood of each point. Naturality and linearity on that neighbourhood make the expressions equal; section_ext concludes global equality. Form a sheaf-of-modules morphism with homMk. Its underlying additive-sheaf map is an isomorphism since every basis component is bijective, by isIso_iff_isIso_basis. The forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, giving the desired module-sheaf isomorphism.
